title: resources
responsibility: Documents shared admission, reserve floors, priorities and the distinction between running work and new admissions.

outputs.name: resourcesGuide
outputs.description: The resourcesGuide value is a fixed Guide literal for the resources topic, listed in the guide index (development-tooling/guide.ts), and it matters when someone needs the rules for priorities, reserves, queue waiting, timeouts and cancellation of local CPU and memory work. It is text only, so it cannot report live load, reserves or queue state; its stated defaults (10% CPU reserve, the larger of 10% RAM or 2048 MiB, 30-minute queue wait, six-hour execution timeout) are not enforced by this module, and admission uses estimates rather than OS hard quotas.

examples.summary: Coordinate coding, tests and background verification across local Harness sessions.
steps: Inspect harness resources status --json for overall CPU usage, usable cores, available memory and queued reservations.
Queue coding commands with priority coding; agent-needed tests use agent-test and background checks use environment.
Estimate peak additional CPU cores and RAM with --cpus and --memory-mib, or use auto for worker-limited standard commands.
Raise reserves with harness resources configure; defaults are 10% CPU and the larger of 10% RAM or 2048 MiB.
rules: One private SQLite queue coordinates all worktrees using the same HARNESS_RESOURCES_HOME (default ~/.codex/harness/resources).

Admission subtracts reservations as well as observed host load; agent-test precedes coding, then environment, FIFO among eligible requests within each priority; nested work skips blocked ancestor pools so running parents can finish.
A running test finishes under pressure. Later work waits; unavailable, stale or pressured telemetry blocks admission.
Nested commands share a validated bounded parent budget. Standard Vitest workers and Rust/Go/OpenMP/Xcode build workers inherit that budget.
Harness verification checks, loop evaluators, Desktop agent turns and repository build/test/check scripts use admission automatically.

On macOS, full checks and managed browser or E2E suites share one heavy test lane on smaller hosts and two lanes on hosts with at least 10 cores. A one-minute load of 15 or five-minute load above 1.5 times the core count delays new heavy work.
Heavy test commands use agent-test priority on macOS. Managed agent-test commands and their children run at nice +10 or lower priority under the Darwin background policy.
Use resources run --heavy-test for heavy test commands outside the standard Harness entry points.
macOS uses VM counters and memory pressure; Linux uses MemAvailable, affinity and cgroup-v2 quotas. Unsupported monitoring fails closed.
Queue waiting defaults to 30 minutes; execution --timeout defaults to six hours. Cancellation cleans owned work only.
antiPatterns: Admission uses resource estimates, not OS hard quotas: external apps and under-estimated commands can still consume the reserve.
Raw commands launched outside Harness are not controlled. Wrap them with resources run; preserve inherited resource context.
Do not suspend running tests, kill unrelated sessions or point each session at a separate queue home.
exampleCommands: harness resources run --priority coding --cpus 2 --memory-mib 2048 -- codex exec "Implement the component contract"
harness resources run --priority agent-test --cpus auto --memory-mib auto -- bun run test
